newsitem.title: FRANCE: French company Cafes Excella to raise retail price.
newsitem.headline: French company Cafes Excella to raise retail price.

text.p: French Cafes Excella SA, a distributor brand that has a five percent market share, told Reuters that it planned to raise retail prices by 23 to 24 percent at end February-early March.
Marketing director Jean-Jacques Dothee said this meant the price of a 250 gram-pack would increase by "at least two francs".
He said arabica prices had risen sharply since December and the dollar was strong.
Dothee also said that if the current rally in coffee futures continued further hikes in retail prices could not be ruled out.
"If the rise continues, we are headed for a second round of retail prices hikes in April," he said.

Industry sources said earlier Kraft Jacobs Suchard, part of the Philip Morris group, will raise the retail prices for its roasted arabica coffees by four francs per kilo, effective February 24. Kraft Jacobs Suchard (KJS) officials could not be immediately reached for confirmation.

London robusta coffee futures are now 40 percent higher than a month ago at $1,680 a tonne while higher-quality arabica coffee ended at a 20-month high on the March contract at 158.65 cents on Monday in New York.
The latest price surge was sparked by fears a strike in Colombia may further curb already tight supplies. -- Dominique Vidalon, Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
